newsitem.title: GERMANY: Boetsch says Bonn mulling fast Telekom sale.
newsitem.headline: Boetsch says Bonn mulling fast Telekom sale.

text.p: German postal minister Wolfgang Boetsch said on Wednesday the government was considering plans to quickly sell its stake in Deutsche Telekom AG.

Boetsch told a news conference in Bonn that the government, which holds a 74 percent stake, was looking at different ways to further privatise Telekom including "unloading the whole package" on a strategic partner.

Boetch declined to comment on reports attributed to coalition sources that Boetsch and Finance Minister Theo Waigel want to sell 287 million of the government's 2.03 billion shares on the bourse this year.
Boetsch said it was not yet clear which model would be used.
He said a change in laws would be necessary to float Telekom shares this year. He said approval for that from the Telekom management board would not be required.
Boetsch said that the government would keep the interests of small shareholders in mind when making its decision.
The government originally planned to keep its 74 percent stake in Telekom until 2000.
A Telekom spokesman said that the government can only sell its shares before the year 2000 in a way that would not affect capital markets.

Government sources on Tuesday said Bonn was considering selling 287 million shares this year and the remainder by the end of 1998. Telekom confirmed the company was holding talks with the finance ministry.
Boetsch added that how state-owned shares in the German telephone monopoly would be sold had not yet been decided, but he was looking at three options:
-- A bourse flotation, which would not require legislation.
-- The sale of shares to a strategic partner.
-- The disposal of the state's entire stake.
Bonn still controls nearly three-quarters of Telekom after last November's privatisation of a 26 percent stake, which raised 20 billion marks ($11.7 billion). ($ = 1.702 German Marks)
